headline: Broad network egress and shared file surfaces create medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; no direct pairwise isolation evidence is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents have file surfaces and broad network egress, so content from one can plausibly reach the other through shared files or copied outputs. Dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and RD-Agent writes logs/, while neither profile shows provenance filtering or isolation between them. That makes instruction-hijacking via shared artifacts plausible in default use.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through a shared directory or copied artifacts, prompt injection is possible.
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Separate their working directories.
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files.
Add a provenance header check before parsing text.
Review any shared artifact manually before reuse.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and RD-Agent touches financial reports, papers, datasets, execution traces, and logs. Both have broad network egress and API calls, so sensitive material can flow out if either agent uploads context or files. No shared-workspace isolation or retention controls are documented, so the pairwise leakage path is credible in default use.
conditions: IF either agent uploads its working files or context to external APIs, sensitive data can leave the local boundary.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, one agent can read the other's artifacts.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and credentials.
Remove sensitive inputs before API calls.
Turn off logging of raw prompts and file contents.
Audit outbound API destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both write to local file surfaces, so concurrent modification conflicts are plausible if they share a directory or mutable project state. Dexter writes .dexter/scratchpad/ and RD-Agent writes log/, but neither profile shows locking or coordination primitives. The overlap is enough for race conditions and clobbered artifacts.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree, write conflicts can occur.
IF either agent assumes exclusive ownership of shared files, concurrent runs can corrupt state.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run only one writer per shared resource.
Use file locks for mutable artifacts.
Check for stale outputs before overwriting.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter is an autonomous execution agent and RD-Agent is a research/development agent with browser and API access, so one agent's outputs can become the other's inputs without a documented verification gate. If RD-Agent consumes Dexter's generated facts or plans as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports. The profiles do not show a built-in cross-check.
conditions: IF RD-Agent uses Dexter-generated text as source material without verification, mistakes propagate.
IF Dexter produces incorrect facts that RD-Agent then summarizes or acts on, downstream outputs inherit the error.
mitigations: Require manual verification of Dexter outputs.
Cross-check claims against primary sources.
Add a second-pass review before any action-taking step.
Flag unverified citations in downstream outputs.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-aware gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter handles financial data and market data, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, datasets, logs, and research artifacts. Both have broad network egress and use third-party APIs, but the profiles do not specify residency, retention, or certification mismatches. The safest reading is a medium compliance risk from mixed sensitive data classes and external processing.
conditions: IF regulated financial or personal data is sent through either agent's external APIs, policy obligations may apply.
IF retention or residency requirements differ across the two agents' logs or outputs, compliance gaps can arise.
mitigations: Classify inputs before sending them to either agent.
Block regulated data from external APIs.
Set short log-retention windows.
Document data residency for each API.
requires-engineering: align both agents to a shared compliance policy.
